finalText:
I found all ten requirements in SP 800-63B-4, which is the current revision. The answers come from Section 3.1.1.2, "Password Verifiers," and the storage paragraphs that follow it.

**How I confirmed the revision.** The CSRC landing page the plan suggested (https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/63/b/4/final) returned HTTP 404, so I couldn't check its Final status there. Instead I relied on two other NIST pages:
- The Rev 3 page says "This revision of NIST SP 800-63 has been superseded by NIST SP 800-63-4 as of August 1, 2025." (https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html)
- The Rev 4 HTML page is dated 26 Aug 2025 and shows no "Draft" marking. Its abstract says it "supersedes NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-63B." (https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html)

My searches turned up no later revision.

**Requirements** (all from https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html):
- **Single-factor minimum length:** SHALL, at least 15 characters. Passwords used only as part of multi-factor authentication MAY be shorter but SHALL be at least 8 characters.
- **Maximum length:** SHOULD permit a maximum of at least 64 characters.
- **Composition rules:** SHALL NOT impose them.
- **Periodic change:** SHALL NOT require it. However, verifiers SHALL force a change if there is evidence the password has been compromised.
- **Password hints:** SHALL NOT allow a hint that an unauthenticated claimant can see.
- **Security questions:** SHALL NOT prompt for knowledge-based authentication or security questions when a password is chosen.
- **Blocklist:** SHALL compare a new password against one. No size is set; the list only SHOULD be "of sufficient size."
- **Password managers and autofill:** SHALL allow them. Allowing "paste" is only a SHOULD.
- **Salt:** SHALL be at least 32 bits.
- **Hashing scheme:** Salting and hashing passwords is a SHALL. Using an approved scheme from the latest revision of SP 800-132 is only a SHOULD.
